stanzas: Little lamb, who made thee?
Does thou know who made thee,
Gave thee life, and bid thee feed
By the stream and o’er the mead;
Gave thee clothing of delight,
Softest clothing, woolly, bright;
Gave thee such a tender voice,
Making all the vales rejoice?
Little lamb, who made thee?
Does thou know who made thee?
Little lamb, I’ll tell thee;
Little lamb, I’ll tell thee:
He is callèd by thy name,
For He calls Himself a Lamb.
He is meek, and He is mild,
He became a little child.
I a child, and thou a lamb,
We are callèd by His name.
Little lamb, God bless thee!
Little lamb, God bless thee!
THE LITTLE BLACK BOY
My mother bore me in the southern wild,
And I am black, but O my soul is white!
White as an angel is the English child,
But I am black, as if bereaved of light.
My mother taught me underneath a tree,
And, sitting down before the heat of day,
She took me on her lap and kissèd me,
And, pointing to the East, began to say:
‘Look on the rising sun: there God does live,
And gives His light, and gives His heat away,
And flowers and trees and beasts and men receive
Comfort in morning, joy in the noonday.
‘And we are put on earth a little space,
That we may learn to bear the beams of love;
And these black bodies and this sunburnt face
Are but a cloud, and like a shady grove.
‘For, when our souls have learned the heat to bear,
The cloud will vanish, we shall hear His voice,
Saying, “Come out from the grove, my love and care,
And round my golden tent like lambs rejoice.”’
Thus did my mother say, and kissed me,
And thus I say to little English boy.
When I from black, and he from white cloud free,
And round the tent of God like lambs we joy,
I’ll shade him from the heat till he can bear
To lean in joy upon our Father’s knee;
And then I’ll stand and stroke his silver hair,
And be like him, and he will then love me.
THE BLOSSOM
Merry, merry sparrow!
Under leaves so green
A happy blossom
Sees you, swift as arrow,
Seek your cradle narrow,
Near my bosom.
Pretty, pretty robin!
Under leaves so green
A happy blossom
Hears you sobbing, sobbing,
Pretty, pretty robin,
Near my bosom.
THE CHIMNEY-SWEEPER
When my mother died I was very young,
And my father sold me while yet my tongue
Could scarcely cry ‘Weep! weep! weep! weep!’
So your chimneys I sweep, and in soot I sleep.
There’s little Tom Dacre, who cried when his head,
That curled like a lamb’s back, was shaved; so I said,
‘Hush, Tom! never mind it, for, when your head’s bare,
You know that the soot cannot spoil your white hair.’
And so he was quiet, and that very night,
As Tom was a-sleeping, he had such a sight!—
That thousands of sweepers, Dick, Joe, Ned, and Jack,
Were all of them locked up in coffins of black.
And by came an angel, who had a bright key,
And he opened the coffins, and set them all free;
Then down a green plain, leaping, laughing, they run
And wash in a river, and shine in the sun.
Then naked and white, all their bags left behind,

stanzas: Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?
Thou art more lovely and more temperate:
Rough winds do shake the darling buds of May,
And summer's lease hath all too short a date;
Sometime too hot the eye of heaven shines,
And often is his gold complexion dimm'd;
And every fair from fair sometime declines,
By chance, or nature's changing course, untrimm'd;
But thy eternal summer shall not fade,
Nor lose possession of that fair thou ow'st,
Nor shall death brag thou wander'st in his shade,
When in eternal lines to time thou grow'st:
So long as men can breathe, or eyes can see,
So long lives this, and this gives life to thee.

passages.title: In Defense of Wild Urban Forests
passages.body: Modern municipal planners increasingly favor highly managed parklands, yet spontaneous urban wilderness offers unparalleled ecological benefits. When native vegetation is permitted to flourish without constant manicuring, microclimates stabilize and local biodiversity expands exponentially. Unmanaged green spaces act as resilient biological corridors, providing essential refuge for pollinators, migratory birds, and subterranean organisms that cannot survive in manicured turf grass. Furthermore, the minimalist maintenance required by wild pockets significantly reduces municipal expenditure on fossil-fuel-powered mowers, chemical fertilizers, and artificial irrigation. Critics often contend that unkempt foliage signals civic neglect or invites safety hazards, but thoughtful minimal intervention easily resolves these visual concerns. Integrating designated unmanaged zones into city blueprints fosters ecological stability while reconnecting urban residents with authentic natural processes. Embracing ecological spontaneity ultimately transforms sterile metropolitan landscapes into vibrant, self-sustaining ecosystems that benefit both wildlife and human inhabitants long into the future.

passages.title: The Necessity of Structured Public Parks
passages.body: While untamed urban greenery possesses undeniable ecological appeal, structured public parks remain essential for meeting the diverse recreational and accessibility demands of dense human populations. Precision-engineered green spaces feature illuminated walkways, wheelchair-accessible paths, and designated sports facilities that encourage active community participation and equitable public access. Uncontrolled botanical growth frequently impedes visibility, creates physical barriers for mobility-impaired citizens, and increases safety risks along pedestrian thoroughfares. Moreover, manicured lawns and curated botanical gardens serve as vital social venues for community gatherings, cultural festivals, and recreational athletics that wild thickets simply cannot accommodate. Effective municipal governance requires balancing environmental goals with human usability. Rather than surrendering valuable urban acreage to unregulated wilderness, city councils should prioritize multifunctional, carefully maintained park designs. These tailored spaces maximize human well-being, foster inclusive social cohesion, and ensure safety without sacrificing essential aesthetic appeal or baseline ecological functionality.

passages.title: The Case for Algorithmic Learning
passages.body: Integrating artificial intelligence platforms into high school curricula offers unprecedented opportunities for personalized education. Adaptive software analyzes individual student response patterns in real time, immediately calibrating task difficulty to target specific learning gaps. This continuous diagnostic feedback prevents struggling learners from falling behind while offering advanced students challenging extension materials. Furthermore, automated grading routines liberate secondary teachers from administrative burdens, allowing educators to dedicate more classroom hours to direct instruction, small-group mentoring, and creative project facilitation. Interactive digital modules also cultivate essential technological fluency, preparing graduates for an increasingly digitized global workforce. While skeptics warn against overreliance on screens, digital integration does not replace human educators; rather, it empowers them with actionable data. By embracing algorithmic learning tools, secondary institutions can dismantle traditional one-size-fits-all academic models, fostering equitable skill mastery, heightening intellectual engagement, and driving measurable academic growth across diverse student demographics.

passages.title: Preserving the Humanist Classroom
passages.body: The rapid acceleration of digital instruction in secondary schools poses significant risks to cognitive development and meaningful interpersonal engagement. Excessive dependence on automated learning software reduces complex intellectual exploration to algorithmic prompts and standardized multiple-choice interactions. This mechanized structure diminishes critical thinking, stifles creative synthesis, and erodes the deep focus necessary for analyzing nuanced texts. Furthermore, replacing collaborative, teacher-led discussions with individualized screen time undermines socio-emotional growth, fostering isolation among adolescents during pivotal developmental years. Essential human capacities—such as empathy, Socratic dialogue, and spontaneous debate—cannot be replicated by sophisticated algorithms or diagnostic software. Educational leaders must recognize that technological efficiency is not synonymous with pedagogical quality. Safeguarding the secondary classroom requires limiting digital distractions and recentering educational practice on dynamic human dialogue, expert mentorship, and physical community. passages.title: The Case for Spontaneous Urban Rewilding
passages.body: Modern municipal planning historically prioritized strict symmetry, manicured lawns, and chemically controlled flora. However, allowing spontaneous rewilding within city perimeters fundamentally transforms urban ecosystems. When native shrubs, untamed grasslands, and unpruned trees expand into abandoned lots, biodiversity surges dramatically. Insect populations recover rapidly, creating robust food chains for urban birds and small mammals. Crucially, unmanaged soil absorbs stormwater far more effectively than hardscaped surfaces or tightly compacted turf, mitigating localized flooding during heavy downpours. Critics often argue that untamed spaces look unkempt or signal civic neglect. Yet, this visual shift reflects a necessary ecological literacy. By surrendering human dominance over every square meter of green space, municipalities foster resilient natural micro-habitats that cool ambient city temperatures, sequester carbon, and reconnect residents with genuine wilderness. Embracing controlled aesthetic disarray ultimately yields profound ecological dividends that structured, highly maintained traditional parks simply cannot match.

passages.title: The Necessity of Purposeful Landscape Design

Unmanaged green zones frequently encourage invasive botanical species that choke out fragile native flora, reducing real biodiversity over time. Furthermore, dense unpruned undergrowth often limits human accessibility, creates perceived safety hazards, and restricts public recreation. Purposefully designed public parks balance ecological functionality with human community needs. By using thoughtful landscape architecture, cities can incorporate native drought-resistant plants, permeable paving, and strategic tree canopies while maintaining clean sightlines and structured paths. This deliberate intervention ensures equal physical access for children, elderly residents, and individuals with mobility impairments. Urban land is inherently scarce and must serve diverse civic functions. Relying on passive rewilding risks creating hazardous, inaccessible, and weed-dominated lots rather than inclusive, functional, and durable ecological sanctuaries for all citizens.

passages.title: An Ecological Imperative
passages.body: Off-world resource extraction presents a transformative opportunity to alleviate severe ecological strain on Earth. Terrestrial mining causes devastating deforestation, soil contamination, and massive carbon emissions, eroding biodiversity worldwide. By transitioning our procurement of critical industrial metals—such as platinum, nickel, and cobalt—to near-Earth asteroids, humanity can preserve vulnerable terrestrial ecosystems. Beyond immediate conservation, asteroid materials could fuel orbital manufacturing hubs, enabling heavy industrial processes to relocate entirely into space. Opponents raise valid concerns regarding astronomical capital investments and complex technological hurdles, yet these initial hurdles pale beside the long-term environmental dividends. Investing heavily in off-world infrastructure ensures our biosphere is shielded from continuous industrial depletion. With proper international regulatory frameworks, space mining will not only safeguard terrestrial habitats but also secure essential raw materials required for green technology, ultimately fostering a sustainable global economy for generations to come.

passages.title: A Dangerous Distraction

Furthermore, the absence of enforceable international governance raises severe geopolitical risks. Unregulated competition over lucrative celestial bodies could easily trigger militarized disputes among spacefaring nations seeking exclusive access. The Outer Space Treaty remains dangerously vague regarding private resource ownership, leaving critical legal ambiguities unaddressed. Rather than pursuing speculative extraterrestrial solutions that primarily benefit elite private aerospace corporations, humanity must focus capital on immediate terrestrial environmental remediation and equitable resource stewardship. stanzas: My heart leaps up when I behold
A Rainbow in the sky:
So was it when my life began;
So is it now I am a Man;
So be it when I shall grow old,
Or let me die!
The Child is Father of the Man;
And I could wish my days to be
Bound each to each by natural piety.
5. _WRITTEN IN MARCH_,
While resting on the Bridge at the Foot of Brother's Water.
The cook is crowing,
The stream is flowing,
The small birds twitter,
The lake doth glitter,
The green field sleeps in the sun;
The oldest and youngest
Are at work with the strongest;
The cattle are grazing,
Their heads never raising;
There are forty feeding like one!                        10
Like an army defeated
The Snow hath retreated,
And now doth fare ill
On the top of the bare hill;
The Plough-boy is whooping--anon--anon:
There's joy in the mountains;
There's life in the fountains;
Small clouds are sailing,
Blue sky prevailing;
The rain is over and gone!                               20
6. _THE SMALL CELANDINE_.
Common Pilewort.
There is a Flower, the Lesser Celandine,
That shrinks, like many more, from cold and rain;
And, the first moment that the sun may shine,
Bright as the sun itself, 'tis out again!
When hailstones have been falling swarm on swarm,
Or blasts the green field and the trees distress'd,
Oft have I seen it muffled up from harm,
In close self-shelter, like a Thing at rest.
But lately, one rough day, this Flower I pass'd,
And recognized it, though an alter'd Form,               10
Now standing forth an offering to the Blast,
And buffetted at will by Rain and Storm,
I stopp'd, and said with inly muttered voice,
"It doth not love the shower, nor seek the cold:
This neither is its courage nor its choice,
But its necessity in being old."
The sunshine may not bless it, nor the dew;
It cannot help itself in its decay;
Stiff in its members, wither'd, changed of hue.
And, in my spleen, I smiled that it was grey.            20
To be a Prodigal's Favorite--then, worse truth,
A Miser's Pensioner--behold our lot!
O Man! that from thy fair and shining youth
Age might but take the things Youth needed not!
I wandered lonely as a Cloud
That floats on high o'er Vales and Hills,
When all at once I saw a crowd
A host of dancing Daffodills;
Along the Lake, beneath the trees,
Ten thousand dancing in the breeze.
The waves beside them danced, but they
Outdid the sparkling waves in glee:--
A Poet could not but be gay
In such a laughing company:                              10
I gaz'd--and gaz'd--but little thought
What wealth the shew to me had brought:
For oft when on my couch I lie
In vacant or in pensive mood,
They flash upon that inward eye
Which is the bliss of solitude,
And then my heart with pleasure fills,
And dances with the Daffodils.
Who fancied what a pretty sight
This Rock would be if edged around
With living Snowdrops? circlet bright!
